Manufacturers and suppliers referenced across the
[Equipment](../equipment/index.md) catalog. Aquatic timing comes from a small number
of companies, and the equipment sections here are grouped by manufacturer because
touchpads, start systems, lane speakers, and relay platforms are normally bought to
match a facility's timing console. Each product article records which console or
start system the device connects to.

## What lives here

Each vendor has its own page, and this index links to them. Vendors are referred
to by name, and logos are not reproduced, see
[Sources & citations](../about/sources.md). When citing a vendor's manual, link
to the official copy rather than hosting it.

The companies fall into three groups. Colorado Time Systems, Daktronics, Swiss
Timing, and Seiko are the principal manufacturers of complete aquatic timing
systems. International Sports Timing and Superior Swim Timing are smaller United
States makers offering lower-cost alternatives to a full console. FINIS is not a
timing company; it appears here because it makes the Backstroke Start Wedge, covered
under [backstroke start devices](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/index.md).
NovaStar is not an aquatics company either; it makes the LED display controllers CTS
ships with its video boards, covered under [scoreboards](../equipment/common/scoreboard/index.md).

| Vendor | Headquarters | Equipment documented here |
|---|---|---|
| [Colorado Time Systems (CTS)](colorado-time-systems.md) | Loveland, Colorado, United States | Timing consoles (System 5, System 6, Gen7), the Championship and Infinity start systems, AquaGrip touchpads, lane speakers, relay-judging platforms, and the DisplayLink display software |
| [Daktronics](daktronics.md) | Brookings, South Dakota, United States | OmniSport timing consoles, T-7000 touchpads, the HS-200 Horn Start, RTOP relay platforms, lane speakers, and scoreboards |
| [Swiss Timing](swiss-timing.md) | Corgémont, Switzerland | StartTime starting devices, in-block loudspeakers, and the OBL2 Pro backstroke ledge, sold under the Omega brand |
| [Seiko](seiko.md) | Tokyo, Japan | PS-series electronic starters and the AQUA and Full-Frame touch plates |
| [International Sports Timing (IST)](international-sports-timing.md) | Grand Rapids, Michigan, United States | The SWIMSTART start system and an under-block speaker system |
| [Superior Swim Timing (SST)](superior-swim-timing.md) | United States | Laptop-based timing software, the Atlantis start system, and lane speakers and harnesses |
| [FINIS](finis.md) | Livermore, California, United States | The Backstroke Start Wedge |
| [NovaStar](novastar.md) | Xi'an, China | The MCTRL and VX4 LED display controllers CTS ships with its video boards |

Colorado Time Systems was founded in 1972 and Daktronics in 1968. Swiss Timing is
part of the Swatch Group, Seiko traces its origins to 1881, IST has supplied aquatics
facilities since 1992, SST was founded in 2010, and FINIS in 1993.

More manufacturers are added as equipment is documented.
